It fuses a temporal channel with a spatial mouse channel precisely because an advanced bot can forge one but not both, and it reports that the combination is more robust than either module alone against bots built to evade. It also states the operational stake: on the traffic they cite, bots were 37.9 percent of monitored requests.
locator: {"sectionFigureTable": "Abstract; Section 1 introduction and framework rationale; CC-BY open-access copy", "sourceUrl": "https://eprints.bournemouth.ac.uk/36055/1/3447815.pdf"}
claimBoundary: Its advanced bots imitate humanlike movement by construction. A reasoning CUI agent is not trying to imitate anyone, so it may be an easier or a qualitatively different target; that difference is untested and is a question this project can answer.

title: What Does It Take to Detect an AI Agent? Minimal Feature Sets for Behavioral Detection under Browser Automation
claimText: In the paper's controlled benchmark, mouse_event_rate plus teleport_click_ratio produced 100% observed agent recall across the tested evasion levels with 0.994 agent precision; the paper also shows the single-feature regime can collapse into an always-agent classifier.
claimBoundary: These are in-corpus observations under the paper's task/executor design, not a universal minimal detector.
